# parity-fuzz --mode func baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode func --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean (four seeds).
#
# Covers function scoping: `local` / `typeset -a -A -f -g`, what survives a
# call, and the options that reinterpret those declarations.
#
# The mode already existed and ran clean, but was NOT gated in CI, so nothing
# stopped a regression in it. Gating is what makes that clean run mean
# something. `trap` and `redir` sat in exactly this state and each turned out
# to be hiding real bugs once their vocabulary was widened — a clean ungated
# mode is an untested mode, not a correct one.
#
# The vocabulary covered the DECLARATIONS but none of the OPTIONS that change
# what they mean (c:Src/options.c): localoptions (c:189), localloops (c:190),
# localpatterns (c:191), localtraps (c:192), warncreateglobal (c:265),
# warnnestedvar (c:266), typesetsilent (c:260), typesettounset (c:261),
# kshautoload (c:179), multifuncdef (c:207), functionargzero (c:141).
#
# typesettounset is the sharp one: it decides whether `typeset x` leaves x
# UNSET or empty, and only `${x-UNSET}` can see the difference — comparing the
# value alone shows "" either way.
#
# KNOWN GAP, deliberately NOT generated — `break` / `continue` inside a function
# body with no enclosing loop IN that function:
#
#     f() { break }; for i in 1 2; do f; print -r -- $i; done
#         zsh    (break escapes the function and breaks the caller's loop)
#         zshrs  f:break: not in while, until, select, or repeat loop
#
#     setopt localloops; f() { break }; for i in 1 2; do f; print -r -- $i; done
#         zsh    `break' active at end of function scope   (warned, contained,
#                loop continues: 1, 2)
#         zshrs  f:break: not in while, until, select, or repeat loop
#
# In C this is NOT an error. `break` sets a counter and the function return
# decides what happens to it (c:Src/exec.c:6104-6112):
#
#     if (opts[LOCALLOOPS]) {
#         if (contflag) zwarn("`continue' active at end of function scope");
#         if (breaks)   zwarn("`break' active at end of function scope");
#         breaks = funcsave->breaks;      /* restore — it does NOT escape */
#         contflag = funcsave->contflag;
#         loops = funcsave->loops;
#     }
#
# so without LOCAL_LOOPS the pending `breaks` count survives the return and
# breaks the CALLER's loop; with it, the count is warned about and rolled back.
# zshrs requires a lexically-enclosing loop and rejects the builtin outright.
#
# This is architectural, not a missing branch: zshrs compiles loops to VM jumps
# resolved at compile time, where C unwinds a runtime counter across the call
# boundary. Wiring it up needs break/continue to propagate out of a function
# call frame. Left alone rather than half-fixed.
#
# ALSO NOT GATEABLE — `$0` without functionargzero. zsh reports its own argv[0]
# and so does zshrs, correctly; but the harness invokes them by different paths
# (`zsh` vs `./target/debug/zshrs`), so the two can never agree. Verified by
# invoking BOTH by full path, where each echoes its own path as expected. It is
# a harness artifact, not a gap. Only the functionargzero-ON case (where $0 is
# the function name in both) is generated.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
